summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of ProFinance Interior SaaS. 20/20 backend pytest cases pass (auth email+bearer+cookie, seed-demo idempotency, dashboard aggregation matching per-project summaries, exact finance formulas incl. sisaTagihan only counting Downpayment/Termin/Pelunasan, worker kasbon/pelunasan tx categories, premium gating 403 -> upgrade unlocks, workitems/progress-summary S-curve with planned+actual, report structure with tukang grouping, report/pdf via ?auth= token returns valid application/pdf starting with %PDF). Frontend: login (Bahasa Indonesia), dashboard KPI cards & health-badge project cards, project detail 4 tabs, cash flow add-transaction, tukang add + kasbon/pelunasan buttons, premium user sees S-curve chart + Export PDF, free user (fresh register) sees paywall banners on Progress & Report tabs, /pricing upgrade modal with QRIS/Bank/E-wallet + confirm payment successfully upgrades to premium.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: report/pdf route calls `await require_premium(user)` — works because require_premium accepts a user dict, but it's using the dependency function outside FastAPI DI which is fragile. Consider a plain helper `ensure_premium(user)` for clarity.
_user_from_request_or_query duplicates the auth resolution logic already in get_current_user — extract a shared token resolver to avoid drift (cookie vs bearer vs query).

server.py compute_summary is invoked N+1 times in GET /projects and /dashboard (one Mongo find per project). For users with many projects this is O(N) round-trips; batch aggregate via $group would scale better.
server.py: `set_session_cookie` sends the cookie but frontend cross-site (preview subdomain) also stores pf_token in localStorage — good redundancy; keep documented.
auth cookie SameSite/Secure attributes should be verified for production; not tested here.

compute_worker returns worker dict merged with computed fields but relies on unique tukang names within a project — if two tukang share the same name their kasbon/pelunasan totals collide. Recommend enforcing unique name per project or using worker_id in the transaction category.
test_credentials: furnitrue.mail@gmail.com / Password123 (premium, seeded). Free tests use ephemeral registered accounts.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests register a fresh user each run and call /api/seed-demo; frontend free-flow test also registers ephemeral user and seeds demo. Premium seeded account is used as-is.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest MUST run serially: use `python -m pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -n 0 --junitxml=...`. The pytest.ini enforces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`, which splits classes to different workers and breaks the session-scoped `fresh_user` fixture (each worker registers its own user). Passing `-n 0` overrides addopts and all 20 tests pass. The `menu-toggle-tier` dropdown item lives inside a Radix portal that only renders after clicking `user-menu-trigger`; if a toast is showing over the header, the click can be swallowed — prefer registering a fresh free user via API to test paywall (as done here).
rca of the issue: N/A — no failing functionality. Only note: pytest-xdist with session-scoped fixtures + class-based test grouping produces duplicate sessions across workers; unrelated to app code.
